newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil press slams Argentina's Mercosur gripes.
newsitem.headline: Brazil press slams Argentina's Mercosur gripes.

text.p: The Brazilian press blasted Argentina Wednesday for blaming its own economic woes on Brazil's Mercosur trade policy.
"Argentina wants Brazil to resolve economic problems which are, in fact, its own," O Estado de Sao Paulo daily said in an editorial. "The problem is not here; it's there."
Argentine officials, upset at Brazil's foot-dragging in implementing Mercosur rules, trooped to Brasilia this week with a laundry list of complaints on export subsidies to financial restrictions.

O Estado said Buenos Aires was overreacting to a drop in its monthly bilateral trade surplus with Brazil, adding Argentina should not expect Brazil to continue effectively pouring dollars into its economy via the trade imbalance.

"It is not reasonable that Brazil, through a permanent deficit in its trade balance with Argentina, end up financing that country's imports from the United States," businessman Luis Fernando Furlan wrote in a column in Gazeta Mercantil newspaper.
"Mercosur is supposed to benefit its members, not third parties," said Furlan, who is head of the Sao Paulo Industry Federation's Foregin Trade Department.

The Argentine officials, led by its former ambassador to Brasilia and current trade, industry and mining secretary, Alieto Guadagni, met Tuesday and Wednesday with high-level Brazilian officials to discuss the issues.

Their complaints include Brazil's delays in implementing Mercosur norms, caps on growth of foreign bank units, bans on subsidized corn and rice imports and restrictions on Argentine firms bidding on public works projects.

Buenos Aires is also griping about the reluctance of Brazilian banks to buy Argentine pesos, obstacles placed by state oil firm Petrobras on imports of Argentine oil products and delays in issuing import rules.
